title: DiffusionBee on a 24 GB Mac: Generating Worked at Once, Editing Mostly Did Not
dek: Hands-on test on an M3 Mac with 24 GB. Pictures came out in about a minute; targeted edits to an existing picture mostly failed.

seo.title: DiffusionBee Hands-on Test: Editing Pictures Mostly Failed
seo.description: Hands-on test of DiffusionBee on a 24 GB Mac (M3): text to image worked in about a minute, but targeted picture edits mostly failed.

faq: Is DiffusionBee free and does it run on the Mac?

The vendor says it is free and runs offline. In the test no payment prompt appeared, models were downloaded through the app, and pictures were generated on the Mac. Offline use and network traffic were not tested.
Can DiffusionBee edit an existing picture?
Mostly not in this test. Removing a passer-by with inpainting came close; logo removal left pink patches, and the sky change, the pop-art change and adding a cruise ship did not work.
How long does one picture take on a 24 GB Mac?
The tester puts it at about one minute per picture at 1216 x 1216 with JuggernautXL on an M3 Mac with 24 GB. It was not timed.
Does DiffusionBee show how big a model is before downloading?
No. The Models page cards show a name, a short line and a tag but no size, and the download dialogs show a percentage only.
Why do the FLUX.1 models say the app needs an update?

The FLUX.1-schnell and FLUX.1-dev cards show 'You need to update DiffusionBee to use this model', although the tester had downloaded the app about two minutes earlier. They were not downloaded or used.

Not stated. Derived from the tasks: run local image generation on the 24 GB Mac, then try a real place, brand text, editing and a negative prompt.

disclosure: The tester founded PromptQuorum (promptquorum.com), a content site and directory about local AI apps. DiffusionBee is listed in that directory and has an existing, separately written review page on the site. The notes record no contact with the vendor, no payment and no sponsorship.

verdict.general: Free, local and easy to start: one 270 MB download, a home screen with six tools, and a first picture within minutes once the default model had downloaded. Generating several pictures in one queued run works well, and a good model (JuggernautXL) gave convincing scenes in about a minute each. Weak points: the Models page shows no sizes or guidance, downloads show no time estimate and one timed out, FLUX models are listed but need an app update, and prompt following depends on the model (a negative prompt was ignored). Editing an existing picture mostly failed: only one of six tries (removing a person) came close.
verdict.fit: Mixed. The tester called it the best local image app he had tried and the first picture app that 'really works', and also said the creative workflow he wants (keep this picture, change this and this, step by step) did not work for him. Reasons and his closing words are under 'How the test went'. His closing judgment comes from notes found in the Msty document (see chapter 'More tests and the closing view').

scores: 270 MB DMG, 'just click open'. The first model still has to be downloaded, and that download timed out once.
Models page shows names and tags only, no sizes. FLUX cards need an app update. Each tool can ask for another model download. An import button exists.
Text to image worked and a good model gave convincing scenes. Brand text was garbled, a negative prompt was ignored, and four of six editing tries failed.
No model information inside the app, no step-by-step edit flow found by the tester, Input Strength and Seed are hard to read. A queue and an Actions button help.
About one minute per picture at high resolution and about 5 GB memory for one model (both tester estimates); no speed or time display in the app.
Not audited. The vendor claims 100 percent offline use; models are downloaded through the app. Offline operation was not tested.
scores_note: Scores are proposals derived from the evidence below (1 = poor, 5 = very good). They are the tester's to confirm.
tldr: Text to image worked quickly: a simple circle on the default model, and convincing scenes on JuggernautXL. The app lets you queue several pictures and keep working.
Getting started has friction: no model sizes, no download time estimate, a timeout on the first download, and FLUX models that need an app update the tester had just installed.
Editing an existing picture mostly failed: logo removal left remnants, sky and pop-art changes did not take, and no cruise ship could be added.
quotes: Why doesn't it say anything about the size of the models so I can see what runs on my computer?
That's the difference between frontier models with access to the internet and pure LLMs that are just generating pictures.
The first picture app that really works.

moments_title: Six moments that shaped this test
moments: No sizes, and FLUX needs an update
The Models page lists names and tags without sizes. FLUX.1 cards say 'You need to update DiffusionBee to use this model'.
The first model download failed with ESOCKETTIMEDOUT. The tester reports it was at 65 percent and he had to start again.
The tester's Heidelberg prompt returned pretty but generic castle scenes.
Inpainting removed the readable logo and left pink patches and smeared strands.
With guidance at maximum the clown, elephant and volcano appear. The beach and ocean do not.
Asked to add a cruise ship to a beach picture, the app returned a ship on a deck and dropped the couple.

chapters.title: Download, first start and the first model
items: The installer is a 270 MB DMG from the website. The tester: 'Really nice startup. Looks fake [wording unclear in the notes]. Nothing to be done more. Just click open.'
The home screen 'All AI Tools' shows Text to image, Image to image, AI Canvas, Illusion Generator, Inpainting and Upscaler (list scrolled; more may sit below).

First use asks for a model: 'Download model to get started. You need to download the following models to generate: DiffusionBee Default 0.1'. The progress bar shows a percentage only: no size and no time estimate. The notes say 2 percent after less than a minute; the screenshot shows 3 percent.
The dialog should say how big the model is and how long the download takes.
While a model downloads, other areas of the app can be opened and used (notes).
The first download failed with 'Please check your internet connection or firewall. ESOCKETTIMEDOUT' and the single option 'Download Again'.

The tester thinks his slow connection at the test location caused the timeout. Not verified. He reports the download was at 65 percent and had to start over; whether it resumed from zero was not checked.
'Come on, this is so unprofessional.' After the download: 'Hurray, after download it works.'

chapters.title: The Models page
items: The Models page is a grid of cards, each with a name, a one-line description and a tag such as 'sdxl_base float8_1'. It lists SDXL Base, Juggernaut XL, BluePencil XL, RealVis XL, Animagine XL V3.1, Anything XL, DreamShaper XL Turbo and more. No download size is shown on any card.
FLUX.1-schnell and FLUX.1-dev show red text: 'You need to update DiffusionBee to use this model.' The tester had downloaded the app about two minutes before.

The PromptQuorum directory lists the last upstream update of DiffusionBee as 30 October 2024 (more than a year before this test), and the vendor page footer reads '© 2024'. The project's README lists SD 1.x, SD 2.x, SD XL, Inpainting, ControlNet and LoRA and does not mention FLUX. Read on 16 October 2026; the release list on GitHub could not be read.
An 'Import From Computer' button sits on the Models page. The tester infers that models he already has can be imported (not tested).

He asks why the page shows no model sizes so he can see what runs on his computer, and why there is no short explanation of what each model is for. 'And as no instruction, it is just like the random downloads again.'
A card for Samaritan 3d Cartoon showed a download bar at 1 percent with no size (notes and a small screenshot).

chapters.title: First pictures: a circle and a brand visual
items: Prompt 'circle with green dot in the middle': a white disc with a green centre on a green background. Settings: Default_SDB_0.1, 512 x 512, 1 image, seed -1, 25 steps. Every picture carries an 'Actions' button.

Next, 'a real challenge': a long, structured prompt for a PromptQuorum brand visual and logo. Settings: Default_SDB_0.1, 1024 x 1024, 3 images, 25 steps. The screen shows a spinner, 'Add to Queue' and 'Stop all'.
The three results are black and white boxes and cards with garbled lettering. No readable 'PromptQuorum.com' and no usable logo.
The tester writes 'I assume the prompt failed because that was not requested'. The meaning is unclear in the notes.
He likes choosing the number of pictures and size. What he misses is a speed indication, an end time and 'some entertainment while it's working'.

chapters.title: A real place: Heidelberg
items: The prompt, written years ago for a frontier model: a photorealistic picture from the Heumarkt in Heidelberg looking up to the castle, with birds and a sunrise behind the castle. Model and settings not recorded.
The three results show a castle on a wooded hill above old half-timbered houses, with birds. None shows the Heumarkt view or the Heidelberg castle as such.
The tester expected an image model to know a real place and its angle. He says himself: 'too much expected from this tool'.

'I could have written, do a castle up the hill with a sunset and birds behind. That's the difference between frontier models with access to the internet and pure LLMs that are just generating pictures.'
The difference is access to the internet or to place knowledge. Not tested in this report.
The tester also tried pictures 'other systems might refuse'. The notes say the app 'did not say stop on anything'. The prompts were not recorded and no screenshot exists.

chapters.title: Inpainting: logo and passer-by
items: Opening Inpainting asks for yet another model: 'ControlNet Inpaint', shown at 3 percent, no size.
Test 1: a photo of a pasta box. Prompt 'remove barillia logo' (brand misspelled), with a mask over the logo. The first try 'failed' per the notes.
After a second try the logo text is no longer readable, but pink patches remain and the spaghetti strands are smeared.
'Technically, removing worked, just not putting the spaghettis back together.'
Test 2: a street photo with a passer-by. In the result the person is gone. The tester: 'Nearly there. If you don't expect something and I don't look for it, you don't see it.'
The brand name in the prompt was misspelled ('barillia'). The mask, not the prompt, did the work, so the effect is probably small (assumption).

chapters.title: AI Canvas and image to image: sky and pop art
items: AI Canvas with the street photo and the prompt 'Make the sky dark blue, real summer day' at Input Strength 30. The result was not captured.
'Blue sky didn't work out, or I don't understand the mechanism.'

Image to image with 'make this into a pop art cartoon picture' on Samaritan_3d_Cartoon_v1_s2 at Input Strength 80.02. The result is a softer, muted copy of the photo, not pop art. Tester: 'Pop art also didn't work out. Not sure why.'
This screenshot sits at the end of the notes, after the speed remark, and is read here as the pop-art try. Not confirmed.

A higher Input Strength keeps more of the original picture. Data points: 21.07 and 21.46 changed the picture a lot, 90.13 returned it almost unchanged, 80.02 gave a near copy. Four settings only; the app's own explanation was not recorded.

chapters.title: Clown, elephant, volcano: models, guidance and a negative prompt
items: The tester checked memory use with Samaritan 3D Cartoon. Prompt 'draw a clown dancing on an elephant', 512 x 512, 1 image: a dancing cartoon clown with a tan elephant-like shape fused behind him.
Memory need on this model: about 5 GB 'of my VRAM'. Method not recorded. Apple Silicon has one shared memory pool.

Longer prompt (clown on top of an elephant, beach, blue ocean, exploding volcano) with the negative prompt 'No blue sky!!' at 1024 x 1024: a blue muscular creature with fiery sparks. No clown, elephant, beach or volcano can be made out. Tester: 'a nice result, but not really what I outlined'.

With the guidance scale at maximum (which, per the app's instruction, 'means it should really do what I ask'): a clown, an elephant-like animal and an erupting volcano appear. No beach or blue ocean can be made out; the ground is dark.
'I would say close, close, close or maybe perfect.'

Same prompt on JuggernautXL_v7_f8 (a further download): a clown with balloons on an elephant, a big volcano plume, a beach with umbrellas and blue water. The sky is blue, so the negative prompt 'No blue sky!!' was not followed. Tester: 'Looks great, except the negative prompt was skipped.'

He wishes the window said what a model is, instead of having to look it up elsewhere. A Google answer pasted into the notes describes Juggernaut XL as an SDXL fine-tune for photorealism (see Background).

chapters.title: A photorealistic couple, and speed
items: Prompt: 'photorealist a couple in love on the beach, watching the sunset over the ocean, birds in the sky, some boats on the water, some palm trees seen'. JuggernautXL_v7_f8, 1216 x 1216, 6 images requested. Two results were captured.
Both show sunset, palms and birds. The first has one sailboat and a camera on the sand; the second has several boats but three people on two benches where the prompt asked for a couple.
The second result (Figure 19) is shown here.
'Looks a bit like AI, but well done, well done.' He likes that you choose how many pictures and what size, and the app 'just runs and runs' while you do something else, then you pick the best.
About one minute per picture at the highest resolution; a file of about two megabytes per picture. Neither was timed or shown in a screenshot. 'Not very fast, but it's okay.'

chapters.title: More tests and the closing view (notes found in the Msty document)
items: The Word file for the Msty test also holds notes and screenshots on DiffusionBee. They are used here as a second source. Their date and order relative to the tests above are not recorded; a file-info screenshot dated 14 October 2026, 17:58 suggests the same day.
'Generate similar images' produced four similar beach-couple scenes from one picture. Tester: a nice function; he calls it 'really impressive'.
A PNG saved to Downloads on 14 October 2026 at 17:58 measures 38,733,330 bytes (38.7 MB). Which picture it is, is not recorded.
Image to image on the beach couple picture, prompt 'add a cruise ship to the picture', Input Strength 21.07: a cruise ship appears at sunset seen from a deck railing. The couple and palms are gone.
Second try (long prompt, Input Strength 21.46): a sunset sea view from a deck with a palm and chairs; no ship on the horizon.
Third try (Input Strength 90.13): output almost identical to the input; no ship.
Per the notes, setting the Input Strength to 100 'crashes' the app. No screenshot; version not recorded.

Eiffel Tower prompt (JuggernautXL_v7_f8, 2 images, seed 770465): two nearly identical towers seen from below. The tester says the tower is fine but direction and proportions are off, and the French-garden trees are 'spot on' while the rest around the tower is missed.

New York night skyline with 'add 3 helicopters flying' (epicrealismXL_v8, 75 steps): more than three helicopters are visible. Tester: it 'cannot count till three and created a second Manhattan Island'.

A food photo with the prompt 'make this german dinner into a cartoon style, many colors, really funny': per the notes, the app 'gave me the same picture back several times'. The result was not captured.

The Seed field has helper text that the tester quotes as 'Starting point for iteration. Any number will do. [App?] will pick one if left blank.' He is 'not sure what the value is'. The word before 'will pick one' is unclear in the notes.

With the Claude app, Word, WhatsApp, Chrome and other apps open, he puts memory use at about 20 GB of 24 GB. His reading: 'even on a 24 gigabyte Mac... it's at the limit again'. The real lesson of his testing is VRAM.

'Function-wise and interface-wise, this is so far the best local LLM app tool that I tried... Not sure I need to learn two or three of these functions, which I do not understand what they do.' 'The first picture app that really works.'

Missing: fine-tuning a picture step by step ('this a little bit, this a little bit'). 'Currently it's not working.' He may be mishandling it. 'In a year from now, this will be perfect.' Final line: 'Smooth interface, works with smaller models, really mostly self-explanatory. Great functions that you can hand over one picture to another tool.'
The tester's forecast that local models will stand beside cloud models within a year or two is not tested here.

severity_note: Severity is the impact on a first-time user. Proposed, not measured.

fits: Mac users who want a free local text-to-image tool and are willing to download and try several models.
People who want everything on their own machine, as the vendor describes it (not verified).
not_fits: Creatives who want to take one picture and change it step by step. The tester did not get this to work.
First-time users who expect the app to say which model fits their Mac or what a model is for.
audience.retest: Retest the untested parts (Upscaler, Illusion Generator, video tools, model import, offline use, uninstall) and record version and macOS first. Retest after the next release; the directory's last upstream update is from October 2024, so a release may be some way off (assumption).

background_intro: Not hands-on. The items below come from the vendor's website and the GitHub project, the PromptQuorum directory, and a Google answer the tester pasted. They were read on 16 October 2026 by a web-fetch tool that summarises pages, and were not independently verified.
background: The vendor page names no company or person. It links a GitHub repository and an account under the handle 'divamgupta'. It says generated images may be used as long as the CreativeML Open RAIL-M license is followed.

The PromptQuorum directory lists DiffusionBee as free, AGPL-3.0, macOS only, with about 13,600 GitHub stars; GitHub shows AGPL-3.0, 13.6k stars, 727 forks and 385 open issues. Directory data last verified 12 September 2026.
System requirements per the README: macOS 12.3.1 or later on Intel, macOS 11.0.0 or later on M1/M2. The vendor page says macOS 13.1 and recommends Apple silicon. No RAM requirement is stated.

A Google answer pasted by the tester describes Juggernaut XL as a popular open-source fine-tune of Stable Diffusion XL by KandooAI with RunDiffusion, aimed at photorealism and anatomy, with several versions. Sources cited in it: rundiffusion.com, openlaboratory.com, huggingface.co and others; not checked here. License terms of the models used were not reviewed.
